title: Homotopy invariance of coherent oriented fiber products
statement:
Use small quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, degreewise pullbacks and functor equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a fixed sufficiently large universe. Let $F:C\to B$, $G:D\to B$, $F':C'\to B'$ and $G':D'\to B'$ be functors of quasicategories. Suppose $v:C\to C'$, $w:D\to D'$ and $h:B\to B'$ are functor equivalences satisfying $hF=F'v$ and $hG=G'w$ as simplicial maps. Define the coherent oriented fiber products
$$T=C\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B}D,\qquad T'=C'\times_{B',\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B')\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B'}D',$$
where the other maps to the bases are $F,G$ and $F',G'$. These are quasicategories, and the induced functor
$$T\longrightarrow T',\qquad(c,\eta:F(c)\to G(d),d)\longmapsto(v(c),h(\eta),w(d))$$
is a functor equivalence. The functor commutes exactly with the endpoint projections to $C,C'$ and to $D,D'$. No fibration hypothesis is imposed on $F,G,F',G'$. Empty quasicategories are allowed. In particular one may take $D=D'=\Delta^0$, with $G$ selecting any object of $B$ and $G'=hG$; that object need not belong to the image of $F$.

source.place: Kerodon Remark 4.6.4.4 (Tag 03PN), Homotopy Invariance; oriented fiber product as in Definition 4.6.4.1 (Tag 01KF). Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED in report.md. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags; no Stacks result states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: Put $A=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)$, $A'=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B')$, $P=B\times B$, $P'=B'\times B'$, $X=C\times D$ and $X'=C'\times D'$. Products of these quasicategories are quasicategories: fill each coordinate of an inner horn separately and pair the fillers. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$. Restriction identifies degreewise with the endpoint maps $p:A\to P$ and $p':A'\to P'$ and makes both isofibrations between quasicategories. Indeed $\partial\Delta^1$ is the disjoint union of its two vertices, so a map from its product with $\Delta^n$ is exactly a pair of $n$-simplices. Write $a:X\to P$ for $(F,G)$ and $a':X'\to P'$ for $(F',G')$. The displayed $T,T'$ identify degreewise with $X\times_P A$ and $X'\times_{P'}A'$. They are quasicategories: extend the $X$ (respectively $X'$) coordinate of an inner horn, lift its image simplex through the inner fibration $p$ (respectively $p'$), and pair the lift with the chosen coordinate. The lift has exactly the prescribed boundary horn and endpoint images.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.5.3: restriction to the two endpoints; explicit degreewise pullback and inner-horn calculation.

proof.text: Let $H=h\times h:P\to P'$ and $V=v\times w:X\to X'$. Both are functor equivalences, directly from the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Choose quasi-inverses $k,v^{-},w^{-}$ for $h,v,w$, respectively. The inverse candidates are $k\times k$ and $v^{-}\times w^{-}$. Pair the given coherent unit and counit transformations in the two coordinates. Their inverse edges and both inverse-witness $2$-simplices are the corresponding pairs of witnesses, so they are equivalence edges in the product functor simplicial sets. This proves the required quasi-inverse identities. The hypotheses on the two squares give the exact equation $Ha=a'V$.

source.place: Remark 4.6.4.4, vertical maps on the endpoint and source products, expanded using quasi-inverses.

proof.text:
Postcomposition $u=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,h):A\to A'$ is a functor equivalence. Its inverse candidate is postcomposition with $k$ from Step 2. To check coherence directly, for any small shape $K$ and quasicategory $E$, internal evaluation defines a simplicial map
$$\Phi_K:\operatorname{Fun}(E,E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Fun}(K,E),\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)),$$
whose action on a parameterized endomorphism $\sigma:E\times\Delta^n\to E$ is obtained by transposing $(f,t,z)\mapsto\sigma(f(z),t)$. Here the displayed expression means the evaluation map on $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\times\Delta^n\times K$; restrictions in $\Delta^n$ commute with this formula. Apply $\Phi_{\Delta^1}$ to the unit edge $kh\simeq1_B$ and the counit edge $hk\simeq1_{B'}$, using $E=B,B'$ respectively. The images connect the two composites of the proposed inverse functors to the identities. A simplicial map sends an inverse edge and its two witnessing $2$-simplices to witnesses of the same equations, so these image edges are equivalences. All functor simplicial sets here are quasicategories by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], applied to restriction from a shape to the empty simplicial set. Thus these are precisely the coherent quasi-inverse data of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Restriction to endpoints commutes with postcomposition, giving $p'u=Hp$ exactly.

source.place: Remark 4.6.4.4, vertical map on the arrow functor category; explicit simplicial evaluation action on inverse witnesses.

proof.text: Form $S=P\times_{P'}A'$ using $H$ and $p'$, with projections $\rho:S\to P$ and $q:S\to A'$. The hypotheses of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-equivalence] hold with its $(A,B,C,y,\pi)=(P,P',A',H,p')$: Step 2 supplies the equivalence $H$ and Step 1 the isofibration $p'$. Therefore $S$ is a quasicategory and $q$ is a functor equivalence. The equation at the end of Step 3 defines $j:A\to S$ by $j(\eta)=(p(\eta),u(\eta))$, with $qj=u$ and $\rho j=p$ as simplicial maps. By clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations], $q$ and $u$ are weak equivalences in the Joyal model structure. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] applied to $qj=u$ makes $j$ a weak equivalence. Its source $A$ and target $S$ are quasicategories, so clause (2) converts this to a functor equivalence $j$.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.34: first replace the arrow category after changing the base; equivalence of j by the specified composite qj=u.

proof.text:
The projection $\rho:S\to P$ is an isofibration. For clarity, use clause (1) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] to regard $p'$ as a Joyal fibration. For a lifting square against any trivial cofibration with right map $\rho$, project the square to $A'\to P'$, lift through $p'$, and pair its filler with the prescribed map to $P$. The two coordinates satisfy the pullback equation, so this is a filler for the original square. The lifting characterization in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] makes $\rho$ a fibration; clause (1) converts it to an isofibration, since Step 4 proved $S$ and Step 1 proved $P$ quasicategories. Now [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-base-change] applies over $P$ to $p:A\to P$, $\rho:S\to P$, $j:A\to S$ and $a:X\to P$. Both structure maps are isofibrations and $\rho j=p$ exactly. It gives the equivalence
$$\alpha:T=X\times_P A\longrightarrow U=X\times_P S,\qquad(x,\eta)\longmapsto(x,(a(x),u(\eta))),$$
and asserts that $U$ is a quasicategory. No lifting condition on $a$ was used.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.34, fixed-base change on the arrow-side isofibrations; pullback lifting verified explicitly.

proof.text: The projection $\tau:T'\to X'$ is also an isofibration. It is the pullback of $p'$ along $a'$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] to $p'$. A lifting square against a trivial cofibration for $\tau$ projects to one for $p'$. Pair a filler there with the specified map to $X'$; the pullback equality is exactly the compatibility condition of that lifting square. Thus $\tau$ has the defining right lifting property for Joyal fibrations in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Since $T'$ and $X'$ are quasicategories by Step 1, clause (1) makes $\tau$ an isofibration.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.34, endpoint fibration after base change; direct right-lifting-property calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-equivalence] a second time, now with its $(A,B,C,y,\pi)=(X,X',T',V,\tau)$. Step 2 gives $V$ a functor equivalence and Step 6 gives $\tau$ an isofibration. The resulting equivalence is the projection $X\times_{X'}T'\to T'$. Identify its source with $U$ explicitly: an $n$-simplex of $U$ has coordinates $(x,(z,\eta'))$ with $z=a(x)$ and $H(z)=p'(\eta')$. Send it to $(x,(V(x),\eta'))$. This lies in $X\times_{X'}T'$ since $p'(\eta')=Ha(x)=a'V(x)$. Conversely a simplex $(x,(x',\eta'))$ of that pullback satisfies $x'=V(x)$; send it to $(x,(a(x),\eta'))$. The two substitutions are inverse and commute with every simplicial operator. Hence the resulting equivalence is the specified map $\beta:U\to T'$, $(x,(a(x),\eta'))\mapsto(V(x),\eta')$.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.34, change of the source-product category; degreewise identification of the iterated pullbacks.

proof.text: The composite $\beta\alpha$ sends $(c,\eta,d)$ to $(v(c),h\eta,w(d))$ in every simplicial degree, by Steps 5 and 7. It is a functor equivalence: clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] converts $\alpha,\beta$ to Joyal weak equivalences, and two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] makes their composite a weak equivalence; clause (2) converts back since $T,T'$ are quasicategories. Projecting that same coordinate formula gives exactly $\operatorname{pr}_{C'}\beta\alpha=v\operatorname{pr}_C$ and $\operatorname{pr}_{D'}\beta\alpha=w\operatorname{pr}_D$ as simplicial maps. For $D=D'=\Delta^0$ take $w=1$ and $G'=hG$; all hypotheses still hold for every chosen object $G(*)$. No step selected a preimage of that object under $F$. Empty inputs cause no exception: products and pullbacks remain the displayed simplicial sets, the inner-horn arguments are conditional on a given horn, and both cited pullback-equivalence results explicitly impose no nonemptiness assumption.

source.place: Remark 4.6.4.4, specified induced map and strict endpoint equations; arbitrary-object and empty-case checks.
